overall_judgement: PASS with minor fixes. All 29 references exist and match their DOI/registry records (25 DOIs: 22 Crossref + 3 DataCite; 4 links HTTP 200; 0 bibliographic mismatches). Every [n] has an entry, every entry is cited, numbering follows first appearance (1..29 exact). IEEE form is consistent (initials, >6 authors -> et al., italic abbreviated venues in all 21 journal entries and the NIPS proceedings, doi: tail). Citation support is good: 4 sentences need a citation moved or narrowed and 1 table cell slightly overstates. Main academic gaps: datasets actually used (MERRA-2, IMERG, USGS 15-min flow, Maurer forcing) and the baseline methods (random forest, ridge, Adam) carry no reference; 7 of 9 literature-table rows come from one research group. Similarity risk LOW: 0 overlap with the cited abstracts, about 0.8% of words with the proposal + mid-term deck, about 6.7% worst case with all the group's own earlier documents, mostly the fixed wordings.

citation_support_problem_cases.text: One LSTM trained on hundreds of catchments simulates daily flow better than calibrated hydrological models [1], [2]
citation_support_problem_cases.why: [1] (241 catchments) trained one LSTM per catchment or per region; per its abstract it beats SAC-SMA only after regional pre-training plus per-basin fine-tuning. 'One LSTM on hundreds of catchments beats calibrated models' is the claim of [2] (531 basins).
citation_support_problem_cases.fix: Split: 'LSTMs simulate daily flow well [1], and one LSTM trained on hundreds of catchments beats calibrated models [2]'.

citation_support_problem_cases.location: 2.2 ('NLDAS-2, whose day ends in the afternoon [14]') and 4.2 ('NLDAS-2 at about 17:30 [14]')
citation_support_problem_cases.why: Xia et al. 2012 describe the NLDAS-2 forcing and land-surface models (hourly); they say nothing about where the CAMELS daily NLDAS value ends. The afternoon day end is the project's own measurement (results/day_windows.json, median 17:40).
citation_support_problem_cases.fix: 'NLDAS-2 [14], whose CAMELS daily values end in the afternoon (measured here, Section 4.2)'; in 4.2 move [14] to the product name and attribute 17:30 to the measurement.

citation_support_problem_cases.location: 2.3 ('The rain table's day ends at 08:48 local time ... [5], [6]') and 4.2 ('... about 09:00 local standard time ... the offsets noted in [5], [6], [13]')
citation_support_problem_cases.why: [5] (V4 shifts pre-noon observations back one day; abstract: 'reductions in the timing bias'), [6] (one-day Daymet-Maurer lag in 325 of 531 basins, full text per results/sources_checked.json) and [13] (abstract: 'accounting for gauge reporting times') support day-stamp offsets in general, not the 08:48 / 09:00 / UTC-day values, which are the project's measurements.
citation_support_problem_cases.fix: Attach the citations to the general statement ('consistent with the time-of-observation offsets reported in [5], [6], [13]') and give 08:48 as 'measured here'.

similarity.method: word 8-grams (lower-case, punctuation stripped) of 1,512 report sentences and table cells (23,550 words; title page, TOC and reference list excluded) against each source; a sentence counts when it holds >= 8 consecutive shared words
similarity.reading: External sources: 0 sentences overlap the 23 Crossref abstracts of the cited works (the literature review is paraphrased). Proposal 12 sentences (0.5% of words) and mid-term deck 7 (0.3%): the title and two short phrases. Older group documents Flood_Report_3pages.docx (4.5% of words) and Flood_Report.html (5.0%) overlap mostly through the HANDOFF fixed wordings; union of all own documents 102 sentences = 6.7% of sentences and of words. Reuse of the group's own earlier documents can still be flagged by a similarity checker as self-plagiarism if those documents were submitted or posted (the proposal and the mid-term deck were submitted to the professor); the 3-page and HTML reports count only if uploaded somewhere indexed. Repeating the fixed wordings ('an upper bound that cannot be had in practice' about 28x, the long Stage IV wording 10-11x, 'an analysis made after the fact' 12x, 'The team's own checks are not yet done' 7x) is internal repetition, not plagiarism; checkers do not score it, though it reads repetitive.
similarity.estimated_checker_risk: LOW: expected well under the 20% allowance; worst case about 7% from the group's own documents, plus a few % from the reference list if the checker does not exclude the bibliography, plus common technical phrases
